evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A person's name declared to match his character: 'as his name is, so is he' (weight 7.1); Wealth does not profit on the day of wrath (weight 6.2). Pair score 13.3.

Only in Enlil and Nam-zid-tara (Enlil disguised as a raven): An elder god (En-me-šara) who usurped the rank of Enlil is held captive; A god meeting a man asks 'Where have you come from?'; A high god meets a man on the road disguised as an animal (a raven) and questions him; The man recognises the disguised god ('you are not a raven, you are Enlil') and the god asks how he knew; Anointing confers an everlasting priesthood on the line.

Only in The disbelievers, the help, and the flame: Curse on Abu Lahab ('father of flame'): his hands perish, he will burn in a fire of flame, and his wife carries firewood with a rope of palm fiber (masad) on her neck; Repeated mutual disavowal: 'I do not worship what you worship, nor do you worship what I worship'; 'to you your religion and to me mine'; Foreign daughter-in-law swears to follow her mother-in-law: your people my people, your God my God [contrast between the texts]; When God's help and the opening (al-fath) come, people enter God's religion in crowds; the prophet is to glorify and seek forgiveness.

leads.title: Nabal the fool, Abigail the wise and David's averted vengeance ↔ The disbelievers, the help, and the flame
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A person's name declared to match his character: 'as his name is, so is he' (weight 7.1). Pair score 7.1.

Only in Nabal the fool, Abigail the wise and David's averted vengeance: The soul bound in 'the bundle of the living' with God; A rich man insultingly refuses food to the hero's men at a feast; On hearing the news a man's heart dies within him and he becomes like stone, then dies; The hero marries the widow of a man who wronged him; An outlaw band claims a gift for having protected a rich man's shepherds; The king gives the hero's wife (his own daughter) to another man; God will make for the chosen one a 'sure house' (enduring dynasty); The hero adds wives to his household; Sheep-shearing as an occasion for travel and festivity; A wise woman intercepts an avenging warrior with gifts and speech and averts bloodshed; Every male cut off, idiom 'one who pisses against the wall', 'bond and free'; Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them.

Only in The disbelievers, the help, and the flame: Curse on Abu Lahab ('father of flame'): his hands perish, he will burn in a fire of flame, and his wife carries firewood with a rope of palm fiber (masad) on her neck; Repeated mutual disavowal: 'I do not worship what you worship, nor do you worship what I worship'; 'to you your religion and to me mine'; Foreign daughter-in-law swears to follow her mother-in-law: your people my people, your God my God [contrast between the texts]; When God's help and the opening (al-fath) come, people enter God's religion in crowds; the prophet is to glorify and seek forgiveness; Wealth does not profit on the day of wrath.

leads.title: Sayings on honest scales, generosity and the fate of the wicked ↔ The disbelievers, the help, and the flame
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Wealth does not profit on the day of wrath (weight 6.2). Pair score 6.2.

Only in Sayings on honest scales, generosity and the fate of the wicked: A city exults at the prosperity of the righteous and shouts for joy when the wicked perish; Like a gold ring in a pig's snout is a beautiful woman without discretion; The people curse him who withholds grain, but blessing is on the head of him who sells it; He who troubles his household will inherit the wind; If the righteous is repaid on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner; The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life and the wise man 'takes souls' (wins people); He who trusts in riches falls; the righteous sprout like green leaves; Treasures of wickedness do not profit, but righteousness (tsedaqah) delivers from death; The righteous is rescued from trouble and the wicked goes in his place (as his ransom); The rich man thinks his garden will never perish and the Hour will never come; One scatters and yet increases; the generous soul is made fat and who waters will be watered; Without counsel a people falls; in a multitude of counselors there is victory; and 6 more.

Only in The disbelievers, the help, and the flame: Curse on Abu Lahab ('father of flame'): his hands perish, he will burn in a fire of flame, and his wife carries firewood with a rope of palm fiber (masad) on her neck; Repeated mutual disavowal: 'I do not worship what you worship, nor do you worship what I worship'; 'to you your religion and to me mine'; Foreign daughter-in-law swears to follow her mother-in-law: your people my people, your God my God [contrast between the texts]; When God's help and the opening (al-fath) come, people enter God's religion in crowds; the prophet is to glorify and seek forgiveness; A person's name declared to match his character: 'as his name is, so is he'.
